text:
sophia: Noticing odd S3 access from partner-mirror-bucket. Found CI artifact `build-2026-04-05.tgz` that contains a `.env` with a Vault token (VAULT_TOKEN=...) and an aws access key. Looks like CI uploaded artifacts to a public mirror by accident.
ben: Oof. Which token and which key?
sophia: Token path appears to be for `auth/approle/role/ci-runner` in Vault, token TTL ~ 30d. AWS key id AKIAEXAMPLE belonged to `ci-runner@redwood`. Artifact created at 2026-04-05T22:11:02Z. Partner pulled mirror on 2026-04-06T01:03:11Z (access logs confirm).
aya: Immediate containment: revoke the Vault token, disable the AWS access key, and rotate the AppRole secret_id. Also remove artifact from partner bucket and request deletion confirmation.
devsec: Agreed. Also need to assume potential privilege escalation: we should audit Vault access tied to that token for the last 48h (list operations, read secret/*, sys/ unseal attempts). Start a targeted audit query now.
sophia: I can revoke the token. Running: `vault token-revoke -self` on the token id from the artifact.
ops-bot: ACTION: vault token revoke executed by sophia at 2026-04-06T02:02:10Z. Audit event created.
ben: AWS: disable the access key now and create a replacement tied to a new role with narrower permissions. Use `aws iam update-access-key --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLE --status Inactive --user-name ci-runner` then delete.
sophia: Done: key deactivated. Created replacement key id AKIANEW0001 and updated CI secrets in secrets manager. Old key deleted after rotation.
aya: For AppRole, rotate the role_id/secret_id pair. Use `vault write auth/approle/role/ci-runner/secret-id -force` to regenerate secret_id and then update runners. Also rotate any long-lived tokens created from that role.
devsec: We need to re-evaluate RBAC for CI: currently ci-runner has write on `secret/data/backups/*` and read on `secret/data/ingest/*` — that's too broad. Propose scoped roles: `ci-builds` with only `secret/data/build-artifacts/*` write and `ci-deploy` separate.
ben: I'll create an IAM/RBAC change: make a new Vault policy `policy/ci-builds` and attach to AppRole. Also create an AWS IAM role `ci-artifact-role` with least privilege and force CI to assume it.
sophia: Partner asked to confirm deletions; they said they will delete mirror and confirm in 30m. Meanwhile legal and partner-ops looped in case of SLA obligations.
aya: Audit plan: enable Vault audit device if not already streaming (sys/audit) to S3 bucket `vault-audit-incident-2026-04` and run query for operations by that token: `jq` over audit logs or `vault audit list` references. Also enable CloudTrail lookup for the AWS key actions and S3 GETs.
devsec: Forensics checklist: - timestamped list of reads/writes performed by token - any policy changes in Vault in last 7 days - list of IAM actions performed with the exposed AWS key - list of hosts that pulled artifact from mirror (partner access log).
ben: One tricky bit: backups in cold storage (S3 Glacier) may have been re-encrypted with KMS alias `alias/redwood-backup`. If someone used the Vault token to retrieve plaintext and rewrap to that KMS key, we must consider rekeying older backups. Let's check CloudTrail for KMS:Decrypt events where principal is `ci-runner`.
sophia: I searched CloudTrail; no KMS:Decrypt events from the CI principal in the 48h window. Looks like token wasn't used to decrypt backups. Good sign.
aya: Still treat as high severity. Followup tasks: 1) rotate AppRole secret_id and revoke tokens (owner: aya), 2) rotate CI AWS credentials and enforce role assumption (owner: ben), 3) narrow Vault policies and run token-sweep (owner: devsec), 4) add pre-upload check in CI to block artifacts containing `VAULT_TOKEN` or `.env` files (owner: sophia).
devsec: Also add an audit alert: CloudTrail event for S3:GetObject on partner-mirror-bucket triggers PagerDuty if principal is not `partner-ops`. And create a Vault audit alert: any token use that hits `secret/data/production/*` from ephemeral CI tokens triggers a Slack alert.
ops-bot: TASKS CREATED: rotate-approle-secretid (aya), rotate-ci-aws-creds (ben), vault-policy-tighten (devsec), ci-preupload-check (sophia).
ben: RBAC change plan (short): create `policy/ci-builds` with limited capabilities, attach to new AppRole `ci-builds-role`, update CI config, revoke old AppRole privileges at rollback window. Will coordinate with devs for rollout.
sophia: Implemented a temporary CI lint hook in pipeline to fail builds if `.env` or `VAULT_TOKEN=` detected. Opened PR and enabled on master.
aya: Post-incident: propose quarterly reviews of AppRole usage, 14-day token max TTL for CI, and enforce `bind_secret_id` to IP-restricted runners. Add MFA gate for high-priv tokens issued via human workflows.
devsec: Good. Also add a new automated job that scans public S3 mirrors periodically for filenames matching our artifact patterns and notifies security.
sophia: Partner confirmed deletion at 2026-04-06T02:29:05Z. We have logs of one GET from partner IP 54.123.45.67 at 2026-04-06T01:03:11Z. No subsequent downloads.
ben: Closing timeline: token revoked 02:02; AWS key deactivated 02:05; AppRole secret rotated 02:20; CI pre-upload hook merged 02:40; partner deletion confirmed 02:29.
ops-bot: INCIDENT: CI-ARTIFACT-EXPOSURE-2026-04-06 declared resolved by devsec at 2026-04-06T03:00:00Z. Postmortem due in 48h.
devsec: I'll own the postmortem. Add remediation owners to the doc and schedule a 1hr retro. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
